precepts.text: When Joshua let the people go, every man went unto his inheritance to possess the land; every family had land and an inheritance, and it belongs to the men, with the wives benefiting as Eve did from Adam.
precepts.point: The genealogy follows Boaz, the land follows Mahlon and Elimelech: you inherit land, you do not inherit a tribe, and here both were Judah anyway.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Judges shows how the land was first given: “And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” We all had land and an inheritance. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land. Whoever of those same families is left after the destruction takes place will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Notice it says every man unto his inheritance. Sisters, you're divorcing us and taking half our stuff, but it says every man. Our wives benefit from our inheritance; it belongs to the men, but it is theirs too because they are married to us. According to God, the inheritance belongs to the men, just as the earth belonged to Adam, and Eve benefitted from it because she was helping him.

And the land we inherit is not an acre or something. 1 Chronicles 2 shows Jair “who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, “even threescore cities”. We owned cities. Somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens. We had castles on those cities, winter houses and summer houses.

That is why the land in Ruth had to stay with Elimelech's family. Boaz begat Obed, and the genealogy goes through Boaz down to Jesse and David, but the inheritance, every man's portion from the time of Joshua, stayed with the dead man's line through the seed raised up to him.

precepts.text: She did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal. The Lord clothed and fed us and we turned around and served the devil with it.
precepts.point: The children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, served Baalim, and forsook the Lord God of their fathers which brought them out of Egypt. They served Baal and Ashtaroth. That stubbornness is our history and why we are in captivity.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
Judges says Israel “served Baalim” and “forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt”. Hosea shows how ungrateful that was: “For she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal.”

That is what the Lord did for Israel. He clothed us, gave us land, gave us food and possessions, all of that. And we turned around and prepared it for Baal; we started serving the devil with what God gave us. Baal, Baalim, it is the same thing: the Canaanite god of fertility, storms, thunder and lightning, worshipped in horrible ways, whose name means lord or master. He sounds like Thor. Baal and Ashtaroth have taken on so many names over the ages, which is why we rarely hear of them, but the worship is coming back to light.

Even now it goes on. Just days before this class, thousands of Afro-Brazilians gathered on a Rio beach to offer gifts to a sea goddess, Yemanja, revered in the Yoruba religion as the mother of all orishas and humanity. Brazil is the tribe of Asher. It is the same deity all throughout: “the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven”. Ashtaroth, the queen of heaven, Yemanja, whatever the name. Our people carried that witchcraft with them and kept doing it, even in Africa.

That's our history, and that is why we are in captivity today, catching hell. The Lord clothed us and named us, yet even in 2026 our people are still worshipping the devil, and we wonder why America goes down there stealing presidents, starving people out and destabilizing countries.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech. Molech worship dealt with children and the womb, and we became bullheaded and did it anyway.
precepts.point: The children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, served Baalim, and forsook the Lord God of their fathers which brought them out of Egypt. They served Baal and Ashtaroth. That stubbornness is our history and why we are in captivity.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord.” Molech worship went along with the fertility gods: it dealt with children, with the womb. That is what we were doing, and it is exactly what God told us not to do. We became bullheaded and stubborn and started worshipping the devil. That is how Israel “forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.”

Stubbornness runs through this whole history. “A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” So we have to prophesy against the idolatry and come up out of this foolishness: Christmas, Valentine's Day, which a lot of our people celebrated. It has nothing to do with us. God did not give it to us.

“Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn”. That is why God's laws are taught without going to the left or the right: we know how we got over here, through stubbornness. If we want to be delivered, we have to wake up.

It is how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” When there is no judge, no leader, in place, they go back to their lonesome: the officer's not here, the captain's not here, the Deacon's not here, the Bishop ain't here. If you can't uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, the same judgment is your future. Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” Stubbornness is idolatry; it is satanic worship. So many think they are not dabbling in the mystic arts, but when you are stubborn and rebellious, you are: “sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone”.

precepts.text: Rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Stubbornness is satanic worship.
precepts.point: If you cannot uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction. Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
Judges 2:19 ends: “they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.” Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal. 1 Samuel 15:23 says what stubbornness really is.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry.” Bullheaded, stubborn, is idolatry. It is satanic worship.

That is how Israel gets down: “when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers.” Whenever there is not a judge, a leader, in place, they go to their lonesome. They get relaxed: the officer is not here, the captain is not here, the deacon is not here, the bishop ain’t here, let’s go back to our lonesome. If that is your spirit, you are going to get the same judgment. If you can’t uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction.

Ecclesiasticus 30:12, read just before, gives the remedy: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn.” That is why God’s laws are taught without going to the left or to the right, and without playing games. We know how we got over here: through stubbornness. So if we want to get delivered, we have to wake the hell up.

precepts.text: Sorcerers and idolaters and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone. If you are stubborn and rebellious you are dabbling in the mystic arts whether you think so or not.
precepts.point: If you cannot uphold righteousness when nobody is looking, that is your future: damnation, judgment, destruction. Stubborn goes back to bullheaded, and bullheaded goes back to Baal.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
1 Samuel 15:23 said rebellion is as witchcraft and stubbornness is as idolatry. Revelation 21:8 shows where the witches and the idolaters end up.

“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone.”

A lot of y’all think, I’m not dabbling in the mystic arts. Yes, you are. When you are stubborn and rebellious, yes, you are. It says sorcerers and idolaters. The one who in Judges 2:19 would not cease “from their stubborn way” is standing with the sorcerers and the idolaters, and their part is the lake of fire.

Psalms 78:8 makes the connection plain: “a stubborn and rebellious generation; a generation that set not their heart aright.” “The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle. They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law.” That is the northern kingdom, though Judah did the same thing. Even when they got over here to the Americas they still did not keep the covenant, and that is why Assyria took the northern kingdom and why Columbus and Cortez came: because of the idolatry. The Lord was sick of it and still is, and this is the last time.

precepts.text: Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods; they shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
The angel rehearsed the command Israel broke: “ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall throw down their altars: but ye have not obeyed my voice”. It was given from the beginning: “Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee.” The Most High warned against letting them dwell in the land because they would make us sin against him, and he keeps reiterating that we will be snared and trapped by serving what these nations serve. Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence fell: “their gods shall be a snare unto you.”

The same is true today in the places where we are scattered: we have made leagues with the inhabitants of the land, and their gods are a snare to us.

precepts.text: Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: “Envy thou not the oppressor, and choose none of his ways.” Israel was told to make no league with the inhabitants of the land, and the same is true today in the places where we are scattered. We find ourselves in their sports leagues and bowling leagues, at their dinner parties, choosing the oppressor’s ways when the scripture says choose none of them. That is making a league with the inhabitants of the land, and the angel asks us the same thing: “why have ye done this?”

precepts.text: Take heed that thou be not snared by following them, and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods?
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
Why should the inhabitants not dwell in the land? Because dwelling among them breeds curiosity after their gods. “Take heed to thyself that thou be not snared by following them, after that they be destroyed from before thee; and that thou enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.” How did these nations serve their gods? What is that thing they are doing with that tree, what are they hanging on the tree, why are they giving each other gifts? That curiosity is the snare.

“Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God: for every abomination to the Lord, which he hateth, have they done unto their gods; for even their sons and their daughters they have burnt in the fire to their gods.” The Most High said, “Observe and hear all these words which I command thee, that it may go well with thee, and with thy children after thee for ever”. Israel did not, and the angel at Bochim told them their gods shall be a snare unto you.

precepts.text: What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: “What thing soever I command you, observe to do it: thou shalt not add thereto, nor diminish from it.” Enquiring after the nations’ gods, how did they serve them, even so will I do likewise, is adding to the Most High’s commandments. He said make no league with the inhabitants of the land and throw down their altars; we are not to add to that or take away from it. Israel had not observed to do it, and so at Bochim they lifted up their voice and wept.

precepts.text: The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire; desire not the gold or silver on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Most High.
precepts.point: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: Throwing down their altars meant this: “The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.” Burn them, and do not even desire the silver or gold on them, lest it become a snare. The Most High keeps reiterating that we will be snared and trapped by what these nations serve. Israel did not throw down the altars, and the angel’s sentence was exactly that: “their gods shall be a snare unto you.”

precepts.text: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun; Oshea the son of Nun is Joshua, whom Moses called Jehoshua.
precepts.point: Joshua the son of Nun dies at a hundred and ten years old and is buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim; he was buried in the land of his own tribe's inheritance.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why: Joshua was buried “in the border of his inheritance in Timnath–heres, in the mount of Ephraim”. Why Ephraim? Because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim. Among the men Moses sent to search the land: “Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.” Oshea the son of Nun is Joshua, whom Moses called Jehoshua. So Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, was buried in the land of his own tribe’s inheritance.

precepts.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own understanding; in all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
precepts.point: We see the same today. Brothers and sisters come with theories they think are their own thoughts, but those thoughts were given to them, mostly by the television. You are either going to follow the one true living God of Israel or the prince of the power of the air, Satan the devil.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
When the judge dies, the people just go off: another generation arose “which knew not the Lord, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel”, and served Baalim and Ashtaroth. A pattern starts to develop here, and it shows we are a people that need leadership. That is why we are told: “Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.”

We see the same today. Brothers and sisters come with theories they think are their own thoughts, but those thoughts were given to them, mostly by the television; that is leaning to your own understanding. You are either going to follow the one true living God of Israel or the prince of the power of the air, Satan the devil. Trust in the Lord, and he shall direct thy paths.

precepts.text: I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.
precepts.point: The curse was to be cursed coming in and cursed going out, coming in from war and going out to war, and the same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said”. Our offence is leaving off the commandments to serve other gods, and the Most High has gone and returned to his place: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” Judges is the record of that affliction beginning to come upon our people for turning our backs on the one true living God.

Look at us today: Black Lives Matter, hands up don’t shoot. We cannot stand before our enemies, so now we beg our enemies to see us as people, to see us as human. We wonder why we cannot get anywhere as a people: individual millionaires, yet no infrastructure, no farms enough to set up our own stores and feed ourselves, no distribution, no hospitals, no textiles, none of the things a nation needs to sustain a nation. The Most High stays in his place until we acknowledge our offence and seek his face; in our affliction we will seek him early.

precepts.text: Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.
precepts.point: The curse was to be cursed coming in and cursed going out, coming in from war and going out to war, and the same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them”. What he had sworn was the curse: “Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.” Coming in from war and going out to war, cursed both ways, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.

The same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you. And we are cursed coming in and going out, unable to stand before our enemies, begging them to see us as human.

precepts.text: I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows.
precepts.point: When the judge was dead, they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, ceasing not from their own doings nor from their stubborn way. As soon as we got out of the condition we were in, we went right back to doing the same thing again, because this is a rebellious and stubborn people, even to this very day.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“for it repented the Lord because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.” It was the same in Egypt: “I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows”. The Most High hears Israel’s groanings under the oppressor, in Egypt and in the days of the judges alike, and it moves him to raise up deliverers.

He does not want to see us on the bottom. But we trespassed against his commandments, so we have to be punished for it; and when the judge was dead, we went right back to doing the same thing again.

precepts.text: He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.
precepts.point: When the judge was dead, they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, ceasing not from their own doings nor from their stubborn way. As soon as we got out of the condition we were in, we went right back to doing the same thing again, because this is a rebellious and stubborn people, even to this very day.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” We are the apple of his eye. That is why it repented the Lord because of Israel’s groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them, and why he raised up judges and was with the judge, delivering them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge. The Most High does not want to see us on the bottom.

But we trespassed against his commandments, so we have to be punished for it. And as soon as we got out of the condition we were in, we returned and corrupted ourselves more than our fathers, because this is a rebellious and stubborn people, even to this very day.

precepts.text: If ye make marriages with the remnant of these nations, know for a certainty that the Lord will no more drive them out, but they shall be snares and traps unto you, until ye perish from off this good land.
precepts.point: The nations were left without being driven out hastily, that through them the Most High might prove Israel, whether they would keep his way to walk therein as their fathers did, or not.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“I also will not henceforth drive out any from before them of the nations which Joshua left when he died”. This is exactly what Joshua warned before he died: “Else if ye do in any wise go back, and cleave unto the remnant of these nations, even these that remain among you, and shall make marriages with them, and go in unto them, and they to you: Know for a certainty that the Lord your God will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; but they shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land which the Lord your God hath given you.”

In the course of making leagues with the inhabitants, what else did we do? We made marriages with them, the very thing the warning named. So the Most High did as he said: he left those nations without driving them out hastily, that through them he might prove Israel, whether they would keep his way to walk therein as their fathers did, or not.

precepts.text: The Most High left the nations to prove Israel whether they would keep his way as their fathers did.
precepts.point: Of the children of Israel Solomon made no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, princes, captains, and rulers of his chariots and horsemen; instead of enslaving his own people he built them up and gave them positions.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel; and he said, Because that this people hath transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and have not hearkened unto my voice; I also will not henceforth drive out any from before them of the nations which Joshua left when he died: That through them I may prove Israel, whether they will keep the way of the Lord to walk therein, as their fathers did keep it, or not.”

That is why there were still Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites in the land in Solomon’s day, “whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy”. The Most High left the nations to prove Israel whether they would keep his way as their fathers did.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: The people served the Most High all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great works he did for Israel.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Joshua the son of Nun dies at a hundred and ten years old and is buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim; he was buried in the land of his own tribe's inheritance.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: That whole generation is gathered unto their fathers, and there arises another generation which knew not the Most High, nor the works he had done for Israel, and the children of Israel do evil and serve Baalim and Ashtaroth.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Because Israel forsook the Most High, his anger was hot against them; he delivered them into the hands of spoilers and sold them into the hands of their enemies, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Look at us today: Black Lives Matter, hands up don't shoot. We cannot stand before our enemies, so now we beg our enemies to see us as people, to see us as human.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Whithersoever they went, the hand of the Most High was against them for evil, and they were greatly distressed. Is that not true today? We wonder why we cannot get anywhere as a people; we have individual millionaires, yet no infrastructure, no farms enough to set up our own stores and feed ourselves, no distribution, no hospitals, no textiles, none of the things a nation needs to sustain a nation.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Nevertheless the Most High raised up judges which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them, and yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but went a whoring after other gods and turned quickly out of the way their fathers walked in.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: It repented the Most High because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them. It was the same in Egypt: he said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people, I have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters, I know their sorrows.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: When the judge was dead, they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, ceasing not from their own doings nor from their stubborn way. As soon as we got out of the condition we were in, we went right back to doing the same thing again, because this is a rebellious and stubborn people, even to this very day.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Because this people transgressed the covenant and did not hearken, the Most High declares he will not henceforth drive out any of the nations which Joshua left when he died. This is exactly what Joshua warned before he died: if ye cleave unto the remnant of these nations and make marriages with them, know for a certainty the Most High will no more drive them out, but they shall be snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off the good land.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: The nations were left without being driven out hastily, that through them the Most High might prove Israel, whether they would keep his way to walk therein as their fathers did, or not.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: “there arose another generation after them, which knew not the Lord, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel.” That's what happens when you don't teach your children. “And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served Baalim”. They started serving Baalim, and they're still serving Baalim today in the Christian churches.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

points: “And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers”. Our fathers never knew religions from Ellen White, Joseph Smith, John Smith, or Charles Russell. They never knew Jehovah's Witness, Pentecostal, Mormon, Baptist, or Catholicism. We never knew that garbage. “and followed other gods, of the gods of the people that were round about them”. We started following the other nations' gods. Today it's Buddha, Seventh-day Adventist, Catholicism, and the religions all around us. You'd think something had changed in 2025. Nothing's changed.

“and bowed themselves unto them, and provoked the Lord to anger.” Every time you go into those churches, you bow to those devils, the men who created those religions. Because those are the men who create that religion. That's what that's talking about. You bow yourself to them. You're thinking you're worshiping God. God isn't inside those churches. Nowhere in the Bible does he tell you to be Pentecostal, Jehovah's Witness, Seventh-day Adventist, Mormon, Baptist, or Catholic. “And they forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.” We're still doing the same thing today.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

points: “And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel”. That's what you see today. He delivered us to spoilers and sold us to enemies until we couldn't stand before them. “Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil”. No matter where we go, the curse follows. You were born here; I was born in Haiti. It doesn't matter where we are. The curse is on us because of disobedience to God's laws.
